diagnostic_exit_comparison.interpretation: At this open boundary, retaining the native position is ahead of all three fixed lower-activation diagnostics. This is a censored observation, not an exit-policy selection or profitability claim.

prior_research_disposition.reason: The tighter policies failed frozen validation or development requirements. The current open lifecycle is hypothesis-formation evidence and cannot reverse that disposition.

Recommendation: Keep the V58 SP500 entry, 80-bps venue stop, opposite-intent exit, 100/40/80 completed-bar profit lock, and 24-hour maximum-hold contract unchanged. Reconcile the authoritative venue close when it occurs and continue the separately frozen future-only long-and-short experiment.
Why now: This lifecycle has the portfolio's largest marked-to-original-stop giveback, while actual capital remains open and the lower-activation future-only experiment still has no attributable lifecycle.
Evidence reviewed: The exact V58 checkpoint prefix, the continuous-improvement report, the future-only route status, the exact V58 configuration, the preregistration and first occupied-signal journal, and the prior SP500 profit-lock disposition.
Observed problem or opportunity: The open short is profitable but has no protected profit because its 72.67-bps completed-bar MFE is below the frozen 100-bps activation. This creates a profit-capture question, but every observed lower-activation challenger currently trails the native marked boundary.
Applicable market regime: Exact source-native SP500 fresh15-v3 short lifecycle under the observed completed-15m breakout-pressure entry; no general regime or side claim is made.
Alternatives considered: Close or change the live lifecycle post hoc, install 25/15/10, install 40/15/20, install 60/15/30, add a fixed target, or preserve the frozen native control. The first five would confound or overfit the open observation.
Expected upside: Preserving the control yields an attributable actual close and avoids converting one favorable open path into a retrospective exit rule. The future-only experiment can later test whether lower activation improves both sides after exact costs.
Main risks and failure modes: The open profit can reverse before native activation; the stop can gap; current exit estimates omit future funding and additional slippage; one open short cannot establish expectancy; and future-only cadence may remain sparse or one-sided.
Validation completed: Run/profile/route identity, actual entry fill, venue-owned protective stop, bound exit plan, completed-candle excursion coverage, current signal state, current cost accounting, three fixed diagnostic policy states, and future-only boundary exclusion are reconciled.
Validation still required: The actual exit fill, exit depth/slippage, final fees and funding, final stop/opposite-signal/profit-lock/maximum-hold attribution, and at least one post-boundary resolved lifecycle per configured side with complete policy evidence.
Success metrics: For diagnosis, resolve this exact close without technical gaps. For any later policy proposal, meet the preregistered both-side lifecycle minimum and show positive after-cost net, PF above 1, and positive largest-winner-removed results across causal development and independent forward evidence.
Failure / rollback triggers: No live change exists to roll back. Escalate immediately if the stop is absent or non-reduce-only, run/profile identity changes unexpectedly, execution/funding evidence becomes unreconciled, or a close disappears without an exact lifecycle record.
Confidence level: High on current technical reconciliation and arithmetic; low on economic inference because the lifecycle is still open, one-sided, and excluded from the future-only selection sample.
